forces.title: Sustained Government Capital Expenditure in Roads and Bridges
forces.description: The Union Budget 2026-27 allocates a substantial Rs. 1,21,999 crore (US$ 13.81 billion) to roads and bridges, a 5% increase over the previous year. Furthermore, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways' capital expenditure has surged from Rs. 5,471 crore in 2012-13 to Rs. 2,94,167 crore in 2026-27. This consistent government focus and escalating investment directly fuel the pipeline for new road projects and maintenance opportunities for IN120101 operators, ensuring robust growth.

forces.title: Rapid Expansion of National Highway Network and Connectivity
forces.description: India's National Highways network has seen remarkable expansion, growing from 91,287 km in 2014 to 1,46,560 km by December 2025, with 9,380 km constructed in FY26 alone. The government also targets a 2 lakh km network by 2025. This significant increase in road length and improved connectivity creates new assets for toll road concession holders and BOT/HAM/TOT operators, while also enhancing traffic flow on existing assets, directly boosting throughput and revenue potential.

forces.title: Increasing Private Sector Participation through PPP and Asset Monetization
forces.description: The Indian government is actively promoting private investment through models like PPP, BOT, HAM, and TOT. The Second Asset Monetization Plan aims to reinvest Rs. 10 lakh crore (US$ 115.34 billion) in new projects, explicitly targeting roads and highways for private participation. PPPs have historically accounted for a large share of highway development. This structural shift towards private involvement creates significant opportunities for IN120101 entities to acquire, develop, and operate road assets, leveraging private capital and expertise.

forces.title: Growing Logistics Market and Multimodal Connectivity Boosting Road Traffic
forces.description: India’s logistics market, projected to reach US$ 527.5 billion by 2033 with a CAGR of 10.9% from 2025, is a major tailwind. Initiatives like the National Logistics Policy, PM Gati Shakti, and the development of 35 Multimodal Logistics Parks (Rs. 46,000 crore investment) significantly improve logistics efficiency. This directly translates to higher freight movement and commercial vehicle traffic on roads and highways, boosting toll revenues for IN120101 operators.

forces.title: Adoption of AI for Enhanced Road Network Planning and Operations
forces.description: KPMG in India highlights AI's potential to transform road infrastructure by predicting future mobility needs and designing more efficient networks. AI can optimize road design, traffic management, and asset performance based on real-time data and complex variables. For IN120101, this represents a significant upside driver to improve operational efficiency, reduce maintenance costs, enhance user experience, and potentially increase throughput through smarter infrastructure, driving long-term value creation.
forces.source_title: KPMG 2025 Global CEO Outlook Infrastructure and Transport

forces.title: Increasing Pressure to Decarbonize Transport Infrastructure Supply Chains
forces.description: The infrastructure and transport sector is a major contributor to carbon emissions. KPMG identifies the complexity of decarbonizing supply chains as the number one obstacle to achieving net-zero goals, cited by 32% of CEOs. This poses a key risk for IN120101 operators, as they face mounting pressure for sustainable practices, potentially leading to higher operational costs, investment in green technologies, and compliance challenges to reduce embodied carbon and operational emissions.
forces.source_title: KPMG 2025 Global CEO Outlook Infrastructure and Transport

forces.title: Expanding Financing Opportunities through InvITs and REITs for Infrastructure Assets
forces.description: India's infrastructure growth is increasingly supported by diverse financing mechanisms, including NBFCs and investment vehicles like InvITs and REITs. These instruments provide avenues for asset monetization and capital recycling for developers, while offering long-term, stable returns for investors. For Roads, Highways & Toll Roads, the expanding use of InvITs presents a significant upside driver, enabling operators to unlock capital from operational assets to invest in new projects or deleverage, attracting broader investor participation.

forces.title: Growing Urbanization and Rising Demand for Efficient Road Transport
forces.description: The World Bank projects 600 million people will live in Indian urban cities by 2036, representing approximately 40% of the population. This rapid urbanization will significantly increase the demand for efficient and safe road transport. For Roads, Highways & Toll Roads, this translates to higher passenger and commercial vehicle traffic, especially in urban corridors and connectivity routes to major cities, thereby boosting toll collection and long-term revenue growth.

forces.title: Improved Data Access for Private Sector Project Planning via PM Gati Shakti
forces.description: The government's initiative to provide private sector access to relevant data and maps from the PM Gati Shakti portal for better project planning marks a significant structural change. This enhanced transparency and data availability can enable toll road concessionaires and operators to conduct more accurate feasibility studies, optimize project routes, reduce pre-construction risks, and streamline the bidding process, leading to more efficient and strategically sound infrastructure development.

forces.title: Strong Pipeline of New Road Projects under BOT/HAM/Expressway Models
forces.description: India benefits from a robust pipeline of new road projects spanning various regions and operational models. Examples include the Capital Region Ring Road (Bhubaneswar Bypass) on HAM, multiple BOT projects (Mumbai-Pune, Pune-Nashik, Bharuch-Surat), and several expressways (Agra Lucknow, Nagpur Mumbai). This continuous project pipeline ensures sustained opportunities for toll road concession holders and BOT/HAM/TOT operators to expand their asset base, secure new revenue streams, and reinforce their market presence.

viewpoints.title: Roads and highways progress remarkable, central to Viksit Bharat 2047
viewpoints.description: CareEdge views India's infrastructure journey as pivotal, with roads and highways demonstrating particularly remarkable progress. Significant expansion of National Highways, high-speed corridors, and deepening rural connectivity position the sector as a central pillar for India's transformation towards Viksit Bharat by 2047. This sustained development is driven by scale, speed, technology, and coordination, fostering integrated infrastructure ecosystems and attracting private investment, creating a highly positive outlook for toll road concession holders and operators.
viewpoints.source_title: Infrastructure Landscape: Vision for Viksit Bharat

viewpoints.title: PPPs vital for unlocking private investment and accelerating infrastructure expansion
viewpoints.description: IBEF emphasizes the critical role of Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) in driving India's infrastructure growth. Noting that nearly 60% of national highways developed between 2009 and 2013 were built under PPP models, the report states that properly structured PPPs are essential for unlocking private investment and accelerating future infrastructure expansion. This highlights a proven and effective operational model for toll road concession holders and BOT/HAM/TOT operators, ensuring continued project delivery and asset creation.

viewpoints.title: Infrastructure and transport CEOs express high optimism for sector growth
viewpoints.description: KPMG's CEO Outlook reveals overwhelming optimism among infrastructure and transport sector leaders, with 84% confident in sector growth and 87% in their own organization's growth. This bullish sentiment is driven by the sector's pivotal role in enabling digitally-driven economies and the large, growing pipeline of projects requiring upgrades. This positive outlook suggests a robust environment for Roads, Highways & Toll Roads, indicating strong future demand and investment prospects for operators.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG 2025 Global CEO Outlook Infrastructure and Transport

viewpoints.title: AI offers transformative potential for designing efficient road infrastructure networks
viewpoints.description: KPMG in India highlights the transformative potential of AI in road infrastructure, specifically in designing more efficient networks. AI can predict future mobility needs, enabling the creation of road systems tailored to topography, land use, traffic patterns, and ecological considerations. This technological advancement suggests a significant opportunity for innovation and optimization for road operators, leading to improved asset performance, reduced operational costs, and enhanced user experience for toll roads.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG 2025 Global CEO Outlook Infrastructure and Transport

viewpoints.title: Sustainability integration into capital decisions remains a challenge for infrastructure leaders
viewpoints.description: KPMG's report indicates a cautious outlook regarding sustainability integration in infrastructure, with only 29% of CEOs fully incorporating sustainability costs and ROI into capital decisions. Despite high confidence in navigating regulations, execution gaps persist, particularly concerning decarbonizing supply chains. This suggests potential future challenges and increased compliance costs for Roads, Highways & Toll Roads operators, who may face pressure to embed environmental considerations more deeply into their project planning and operations, impacting profitability.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG 2025 Global CEO Outlook Infrastructure and Transport
